reports.executive-decision-memo.md:
# Olam Agri: evidence before irreversible expansion

Manash Protim Deori | 2026–2051 | Version 1.0.0 | Research cutoff: 8 October 2026, 00:04 IST

## The decision

Approve a scoped 90-day evidence and controlled commercial pilot programme. Finance should first reconcile the data room and approve a costed envelope, cash limits and minimum economically material effect. Defer an unconditional owned-asset commitment. Public data do not establish country-level Olam orders, attainable shares, delivered margins, taxes or funding. This package makes those missing facts visible.

## Why the capital story changes

Olam Agri FY2025 revenue was USD28,666 million and EBIT was USD703.7 million, yielding a derived margin of 2.4548%. Sales volume rose 19.1% and revenue 15.4%, while EBIT fell 8.0%. The annual report, printed pages 10–11, provides this comparable USD company perimeter. Handled tonnage of 49.474 million differs from sales volume of 53.740 million. Olam Group SGD figures and its H1 2026 continuing operations must not be assigned to Agri.

After the 30 June 2026 CFG share issuance, SALIC held 81.81% and Olam Group 18.19%. The About page's lower 81.11% text conflicts with the dated transaction evidence; the conflict remains recorded. Ownership does not guarantee an order, funding or a government procurement preference.

The inherited Nigeria NGN100 billion sales screen produces annual uplift of NGN0.47 billion, a one-time sales-day cash proxy of NGN1.9178 billion, and three-year NPV of minus NGN2.0645 billion against NGN4.2 billion initial capital at the chosen 28% hurdle. It remains a screening case rather than company guidance. Production economics must replace its additive sales growth, overlap-prone leakage penalties and seven-sales-day proxy with measured orders, procurement costs and actual AR, inventory and AP.

<!-- pagebreak -->

## Where to learn

The atlas contains 193 UN members and two observer states, with territories indexed separately. Every country has a current-presence status, product and route hypothesis, entry mode, disposition and next evidence gate. Ten diligence priorities are Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, Cameroon, Mozambique, South Africa, India, Vietnam, Brazil and Saudi Arabia. All 195 country financial cases remain threshold-only, with unknown company cash values left blank.

Nigeria tests semolina and edible oils as separate cohorts. Ghana and Senegal test usable output and service; Cameroon and Mozambique test availability, credit and cash tickets; South Africa examines industrial contracts. India, Vietnam and Brazil test contracted origination and routes. Saudi Arabia requires independently bankable commercial offtake. Existing capability supports a test, without establishing incremental profit.

## Financial discipline

Six unweighted worlds connect orders, costs, stock days, capacity and hurdle rates. No complete 25-year path is labelled most likely. OECD–FAO's 2026–2035 outlook is an external benchmark; extensions beyond 2035 are chosen and bounded. UN WPP2024 medium population paths are external projections, not product demand.

The normalized 25-year project templates use constant 2026 USD, staged capital, commissioning ramps, tax-loss carryforward, capital-cohort depreciation, maintenance, replacement and correctly based working capital. The final year includes 90% NWC recovery and no perpetual franchise value. Managed owned processing has NPV of minus USD1.80 million and peak annual funding need of USD22.56 million. Its operating break-even is 33,333 tonnes, compared with zero-NPV initial annual orders of 104,862 tonnes. These are chosen examples, not Olam or country valuations; monthly seasonal cash may require more funding.

<!-- pagebreak -->

## Proof, governance and leadership action

Days 1–15 reconcile entity and data. Days 16–30 pre-register the counterfactual, statistical power and cost. Days 31–60 test. Days 61–75 verify cash and transferability. Days 76–90 decide whether to expand, resize, wait or stop. G0–G7 cover perimeter, legal access, customers, contribution, capacity, resilience, cash and replication. Legal and liquidity failures override a demand narrative.

The primary outcome is incremental paid contribution after service, trade and cannibalisation, accompanied by sustained repeat and funding evidence. Sample size must derive from baseline variance, the minimum economic effect, clustering and attrition. No actual Olam treatment effect or pilot budget is asserted.

The executed aggregate food-supply regression offers only a small holdout improvement and is rejected for investment forecasting. Chosen stress quantiles are not calibrated probabilities. The proposed adaptive framework applies established regret, causal measurement and information-value methods; it does not claim a new theorem or a validated optimal global allocation.

Request customer orders, gross-to-net prices, product and route costs, plant constraints, monthly inventory and credit balances, tax and FX records. Appoint Finance, Treasury, Legal, Operations and Marketing owners. Authorize a costed proof programme, challenge its release criteria, and return in 90 days with measured contribution, repeat, cash and a specific next commitment.

Source IDs: CO_AR, CO_OWN, CO_FACT, UN_WPP, OECD and BASELINE. Calculation IDs: C-LEGACY, C-DCF-plant-managed, C-THRESHOLD and C-OLS. The companion source, assumption and calculation registers provide exact URLs, pinpoints, units and code paths.
reports.pilot-charter.md:
# 90-day pilot charter and candidate contribution

Version 1.0.0 | Proposed programme; not an Olam approval

Objective: estimate incremental paid contribution and funding for a bounded Nigeria semolina or edible-oils intervention. Keep category cohorts separate; select a transfer market only after feasibility checks. Finance sets the cost cap, cash breach limit and minimum economically material effect before launch.

## Responsibilities and milestones

Days 1–15: Finance and Country Operations reconcile eligible sell-through, customer IDs, credit, product costs, inventory, route service and capacity. Legal verifies entity and product access. Deliver a signed data dictionary and baseline.

Days 16–30: Marketing and Analytics pre-register the design. Prefer randomized route clusters where feasible. Otherwise use credible matched holdouts with pre-trend diagnostics. Specify outcomes, cannibalisation, spillovers, attrition, treatment timing and inference. Determine sample size from variance, detectable effect and intracluster correlation.

Days 31–60: execute and audit treatment, stock availability, paid orders, usable yield, returns, service cost and stock funding. Separate the intervention from other promotions. Pause or stop according to pre-agreed contribution, legal and cash limits.

Days 61–75: measure paid repeat after support ends; reconcile contribution and cash; run one documented transferability test with local pack, yield, route and credit assumptions.

Days 76–90: Finance independently reviews the effect interval, mechanism evidence and liquidity. Decide expand, localise, resize, wait or stop. Do not extrapolate a short-run effect unchanged through 2051.

## Measures and acceptance

Primary outcome: incremental eligible contribution net of incremental service, trade and cannibalisation. Secondary outcomes: sustained paid repeat, customer usable output, delivery reliability, credit losses, DSO, DIO, DPO and funding. Net ROMI equals incremental contribution after marketing cost divided by marketing cost. Multi-year proposals use full cash-flow NPV.

Actual sample and budget remain unset until baseline data are available. Acceptance requires the approved economic floor, documented cash headroom, no overriding access or rights breach, and understood transfer conditions.

## My contribution

Manash Protim Deori combines an MBA at IIM Shillong with chemical engineering. I can own the data dictionary, source lineage, commercial experiment specification and proof-to-cash reporting under Finance's authority. Portfolio evidence of a INR20 million budget and CPM reduction from INR35.8 to INR15.5 is candidate context, not proof of Olam profit. The Meghalaya exercise was a simulation informed by government records; no realised savings are claimed.

Data needed: pseudonymous customer and order records, net prices, returns, costs, credit, inventory, plant and route utilization, tax, FX and hedge records. Owners: Country, Finance, Treasury, Legal, Marketing and Operations.
reports.validation-and-red-team.md:
# Model validation and red-team review

Version 1.0.0 | No investment-grade country forecast

Executed coverage: 195 unique country dossiers, seven UN population milestones, six chosen worlds, 8,190 matrix rows, 18 full 25-year normalized cash cases, order-threshold roots, 2,500/5,000/10,000-draw stress runs, and OLS with temporal and geographic validation. Missing values remain null. Source vintages, checksums, series and units are retained or reproducible.

## Executed econometrics

Training contains 2,856 country-year records from 2002–2018 and 171 countries. The holdout contains 680 records from 2019–2022. The target is annual growth of the food production index, a supply proxy rather than consumption or Olam demand. In-sample R-squared is 0.006179. Holdout MAE is 0.048299 against 0.049794 for country means and 0.048960 for zero growth. Country-clustered CR1 intervals show imprecise slopes.

The model is rejected for country investment forecasts. Latest-vintage retrospective validation is not a real-time vintage backtest. Common global shocks, measurement error and structural breaks remain. No causal elasticity or 2051 product forecast is claimed. Exact coefficients, intervals and leave-region-out results are in the workbook and analysis JSON.

## Challenges and falsifiers

1. Does population imply profit? No. Eligible buyers, capture, price, cost and funding must clear the template boundary.
2. Does SALIC ownership create an order? No. Independently bankable offtake is required.
3. Is EBITDA sufficient? No. The managed owned example has negative NPV after capital and working cash.
4. Is the cash release recurring? No. A working-capital transition releases cash once.
5. Are stress frequencies probabilities of success? No. They describe a chosen generator. Business dependence must be measured.
6. Is the new framework proven superior? No. A teaching counterexample is not an Olam allocation backtest.
7. Do different countries diversify risk? Only if crop, port, buyer, FX and lender exposure differ.
8. Does a country page establish legal access? No. Counsel must check the actual product, rule and counterparty.
9. Does global warming establish local crop damage? No. Crop, basin and asset links are missing.
10. Does CPM improvement prove Olam profit? No. It is self-described portfolio evidence.

## Accounting and physical checks

Revenue equals delivered tonnes times net price; deliveries cannot exceed usable capacity. NWC equals AR plus inventory minus AP. Taxes cannot be negative under the chosen loss convention. FCFF reconciles to EBIT less cash tax plus D&A less capex and NWC change plus closeout. Each capital cohort depreciates over ten years. The terminal amount contains only 90% NWC recovery. Threshold roots are checked against full NPV. Annual cash does not certify monthly solvency.

Production review still needs Finance actuals, Legal access and rights, Treasury currency/hedges, Operations yield/capacity, location-linked hazards and Marketing counterfactuals. Artifact checks are not external business validation.
reports.prior-art-and-originality.md:
# Prior art and originality assessment

The proposal combines established cash-flow valuation, working-capital identities, constrained optimization, minimax regret, CVaR, real options, Bayesian information value and causal experimentation. Primary references include Rockafellar–Uryasev for CVaR and Callaway–Sant'Anna for difference-in-differences. Aglink-Cosimo provides an institutional partial-equilibrium benchmark. Economic Sciences research context includes Engle/Granger (2003), Romer/Nordhaus (2018), and Card/Angrist/Imbens (2021).

The operating proposal connects customer usable-output economics, physical delivery, seasonal cash, common exposure and learning triggers at country, product, segment, mode, corridor, scenario and horizon level. This may be a useful integration; it is not a new mathematical theorem.

Hypothesis one: transferable commercial learning can outweigh macro market size. Hypothesis two: seasonal working cash can reverse a volume-based ranking. Neither has been validated on Olam internal cases.

Benchmark protocol: hold feasible markets, horizon, maximum capital and information constant. Compare size ranking, stand-alone NPV, expected NPV, regret and adaptive policies. Track out-of-sample regret, cash breaches, returns, decision stability and operating complexity. The executed four-action/six-world example has partner maximum regret of 4 versus owned regret of 8, while owned wins the central case 9 versus 6. Its payoffs are chosen teaching inputs, not empirical results.

Literature coverage is limited to the documented primary sources and methods. It is not an exhaustive patent, academic or commercial-system search. No exclusive originality or empirical superiority claim is warranted.
reports.limitations-and-missing-data.md:
# Limitations ranked by decision consequence

1. Product/customer orders, capture, net price and costs can reverse contribution and country ranking. All 195 country investment NPVs remain unknown.
2. Monthly seasonal AR, inventory, AP, purchases, tax, FX and hedges can reverse funding and returns. Annual cash omits intra-year peaks; no Olam WACC is asserted.
3. Legal product access, sanctions, rights, usable capacity, yield and route constraints can eliminate a candidate from the feasible set.
4. Competitor prices, shares, service and responses are unavailable at product level. No invented competitive advantage is used.
5. Basin, crop and facility hazards and adaptation cost are missing. Country water stress cannot price asset loss.
6. Diet, health, product consumption and causal adoption remain unmeasured. Public FAO food-balance bulk access failed; no per-person consumption is imputed. No elasticity or Olam marketing effect is estimated.
7. Panel validation uses latest-vintage WDI, complete cases and a weak aggregate supply model. It is rejected for investment forecasting.
8. OECD–FAO's horizon ends in 2035. Extensions through 2051 are chosen scenarios. UN WPP2024 medium population is an external projection.
9. Company sources contain conflicting ownership text and differing tonnage definitions. Dated transactions and defined annual metrics take precedence. Locations are not an asset register or proof of absence elsewhere.
10. Stress and policy examples are chosen, not calibrated probabilities. No optimal all-country allocation or validated mathematical novelty is claimed.

Each country has a next evidence gate. Failed retrievals are logged and not treated as support. No missing financial input is replaced with a fabricated company value.
reports.reproduce.md:
# Reproduction and navigation

Version 1.0.0 | Seed 20261008 | Public-data decision scaffold

Python 3.11+, NumPy, pandas, SciPy and an Excel-reading engine are needed for retrieval and analysis. Exact execution versions are in environment.json. Run scripts/olam-retrieve.py, then scripts/olam-analyse.py, then scripts/olam-package.py. Public sources may block requests; errors remain logged. Cleaned country-panel, WPP milestones, M49, holdout and analysis outputs are included for review.

Native artifact authoring uses scripts/olam-artifacts.mjs with @oai/artifact-tool in the Codex primary runtime. PDF generation uses scripts/olam-pdfs.py with ReportLab. PowerPoint contains editable text, tables and charts. The workbook has one active financial model and live formulas; scenario and stress snapshots are clearly dated cached code results.

country-scenario-matrix.csv has 8,190 rows, with unknown country economics left blank. Normalized template order thresholds are separate fields. Population projections are in persons. country-register.csv contains 195 dispositions; territories-annex.csv contains the remaining M49 areas. Source, claim, assumption and calculation registers link IDs, units, pinpoints, slides and code. change-audit.csv covers all 44 original slides.

The portfolio route remains /work/olam-africa-growth-strategy. The refresh policy is a proposal; no monitoring automation has been scheduled. Research readiness does not constitute company investment approval.

data-dictionary: Join UN M49 identifiers to WDI by ISO3 and year; observers are VAT and PSE. Territories have a separate annex.
Convert WPP population from thousands to persons. A broad food-import proxy uses food share and merchandise imports from the same year.
Food production is a supply index; real PPP income, urban share and water stress are dated observations, not customer demand.
Complete-case regression uses no imputation. Macro availability does not establish candidate feasibility.
demand-trade-methods: Demand begins with population and per-person quantity by segment; accessible customers, capture and delivery then bound sales.
AIDS/QUAIDS and discrete-choice models need observed spending, prices and identification. No imported elasticity is used.
A PPML gravity module would need bilateral product flows, fixed effects and barrier data. No fitted gravity result is claimed.
Aglink-Cosimo is an institutional benchmark. Its official projection is not extended mechanically to 2051.
climate-methods: A crop panel would link calendar-specific weather and basin conditions to yields, with fixed effects and validated nonlinear responses.
Convert fitted yield or downtime into saleable volume, procurement cost and stock days; price adaptation explicitly.
Traceability and standards affect access and compliance cost. Include a premium only when buyers pay it.
Asset coordinates, hazards and measured adaptation effects are unavailable; financial damage outputs remain conditional.
equations: Delivered volume = min(eligible orders, usable capacity, route capacity). Revenue = delivered volume × net price.
EBITDA = volume × (price − variable cost per unit) − fixed cash cost. EBIT = EBITDA − D&A.
NWC = credit revenue × DSO/365 + inventory cost × DIO/365 − eligible purchases × DPO/365.
FCFF = EBIT − cash tax + D&A − capex − change in NWC + closeout. NPV discounts all incremental cash.
math-methods: Linear algebra supports regression and dependence; uncertainty requires an appropriate error structure.
Calculus and root finding locate margin and NPV thresholds. Capacity breakpoints can invalidate smooth derivatives.
Network flow connects origin, port and customer constraints. Inventory and queues need lead-time and service data.
Optimization, dynamic programming and Bayes structure actions and learning. Priors and transitions need evidence.
validation-transfer: Latest-vintage temporal validation is retrospective. The small error gain and uneven geographic transfer do not justify investment forecasting.
stress-spec: Chosen latent factors jointly alter volume, costs, stocks and rates. Seed 20261008; covariance is constructed, not fitted to country data.
policy-prior-art: Robust regret, CVaR, constrained optimization, causal experiments, real options and EVSI are established methods.
Growth, climate, time-series and causal research guide module choice; no Nobel research parameter is imported into company forecasts.
The proposed integration links usable customer output to seasonal cash and transferable learning.
Only the transparent teaching comparison is executed. Superiority over real country allocation is unvalidated.
pilot-power: For two independent arms, n ≈ 2(zα/2 + zβ)²σ²/δ² per arm. Cluster design effect = 1 + (m − 1)ICC.
Chosen σ=10, δ=5, α=.05 and 80% power imply about 63 observations per arm before clustering or attrition.
With 10 customers per cluster and ICC=.10, the design effect is 1.9: about 120 adjusted observations per arm.
Actual route variance, balance, spillovers and attrition determine the final sample. No actual sample size is approved.
atlas-navigation: The country view links observations and source years to population paths, product/route hypotheses, modes and evidence gates.
Each of six worlds shows a normalized order threshold; country NPV remains unknown.
Seven milestones: 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, 2045, 2050 and 2051. Exact matrix rows are downloadable.
Separate M49 territories are indexed. An undisclosed location is not proof that the company is absent.
limitations: Orders, capture, prices and costs can reverse contribution, NPV and country priorities.
Monthly cash, FX, hedges and tax can create unfunded losses despite positive annual EBITDA.
Yield, capacity, route access and rights can remove a candidate from the feasible set.
Asset hazards, competitors and causal adoption can reverse resilience and transferability.
refresh: Recheck company and ownership evidence at material transactions and results; preserve perimeter conflicts.
Legal rechecks rules, taxes, sanctions and rights before a named route commitment.
Review customer orders and stock cash monthly; escalate breaches immediately and test repeat after support ends.
Refresh data vintages, holdouts and scenarios annually; explain changed decisions, not only better fit.
audit: Preserve customer economics, cash discipline, the Nigeria laboratory and accurately bounded candidate experience.
Repair ownership, tonnage definitions, official projection horizons, procurement FX overlap and working-capital bases.
Expand to 195 countries, six worlds, full cash flow, causal pilot design and a linked technical package.
Replace unverified review counts, model probability claims and implied funding with evidence and actual validation.

1: Using rounded revenue of USD28.7bn gives 2.4519%; keep the same entity, period and currency.
Revenue can grow while margin falls.
2: Population × demand per person × access × capture, capped by delivery
Demand, access and capture are chosen inputs. Unmet orders cannot count as revenue.
If route capacity reaches 9,000t, plant capacity still caps delivery at 8,000t.
3: 100,000t × USD400/t = USD40m revenue; costs = USD34m; contribution = USD6m; less USD2m fixed cost = USD4m EBITDA.
Volume × net price; volume × unit cost; contribution less fixed cash cost
EBITDA omits cash tax, capital spending and working cash. These are chosen saleable-volume and net-price inputs.
A USD10/t price change at unchanged volume changes EBITDA by USD1m.
4: Input = main output / yield; output, by-product and loss sum to input
By-products may earn revenue. Their quality, price and conversion cost need evidence.
At 95% main yield, input is 105,263t. Reconcile the remaining mass separately.
5: Offer A: (USD30 + USD5) / 45kg = USD0.7778/kg. Offer B: (USD32 + USD4) / 48kg = USD0.7500/kg.
Purchase and preparation cost / usable output
B costs 3.57% less per usable kg
Chosen flour-like inputs. Paid adoption also depends on cash, trust and availability.
If B produces only 45kg, cost rises to USD0.80/kg and reverses the advantage.
6: Small: (₦600 + ₦100 prep) / 5 meals = ₦140/meal. Large: (₦2,000 + ₦400 prep) / 20 meals = ₦120/meal.
Cash ticket differs from cost per use; assume 100g dry input per meal
Small cash ticket ₦600; large pack 14.29% cheaper per meal
Chosen Nigerian cash units and serving size. The large pack needs more upfront cash.
Large purchase cash is 3.33 times the small pack, despite lower cost per meal.
7: Distinguish absolute percentage-point change from relative percentage change
A margin change is not the same measure as revenue growth.
On USD100 revenue, profit rises from USD8 to USD10.
8: EBIT less tax, plus D&A, less maintenance/growth capex and change in NWC
Assume no prior tax losses, 25% tax, USD0.6m maintenance and USD0.4m growth capex.
If NWC does not increase, this period’s cash rises by USD1m.
9: AR: USD40m × 5 / 365 = USD0.547945m. Inventory: USD34m × 7 / 365 = USD0.652055m. Total = USD1.20m.
Revenue basis for receivables; cost basis for inventory; DPO unchanged
All sales are credit in this example. The transition release is not recurring annual profit.
One further DSO day releases USD0.109589m at this sales base.
10: Inherited additive uplift and sales-day proxy; ramped three-year DCF
NGN4.2bn initial capital; 28% hurdle; 50/80/100% benefit ramp. Tax, replacement and actual cash bases are absent.
Repair procurement FX overlap, AR/inventory/AP, capex, tax and currency before a production decision.
11: Local imported cost = USD commodity price × local currency per USD
Both shocks hit the same procurement base. Hedge effects need documented contracts.
Chosen 70% cost pass-through recovers 14.7% initially; weaker customer volume may reduce retained margin.
12: Discount each dated free cash flow; do not compare only undiscounted totals
No terminal value. Staging USD3m now and USD2m in year 1, with cash in years 2–4, gives −USD0.2966m.
Paying USD5m now with a one-year cash delay gives −USD0.4784m.
13: Consistent inflation of both cash and discount rate preserves NPV
Real and nominal three-year NPVs both −USD0.0263m
Nominal cash grows by 5% inflation and is discounted at 15.5%. Project and currency risk require separate care.
Mixing nominal cash with a real hurdle overstates value.
14: USD2m / (USD400 − USD340 per tonne) = 33,333t; / 150,000t capacity = 22.22% utilization.
Operating break-even pays fixed cash cost; investment break-even also pays capital
Operating 33,333t; investment boundary 104,862 initial order tonnes
Full NPV includes ramp, tax, replacement, working cash and the finite horizon.
Operating above 22.22% utilization can still give negative investment NPV.
15: Weighted average = sum of chosen weight × conditional NPV
The central USD10m case is not a calibrated most-likely future. The adverse loss can breach funding.
If adverse weight is 0.5 and central weight 0.3, the mean becomes −USD0.6m.
16: NPVs [−8, −4, 0, 2, 6] imply losses [0, 0, 0, 4, 8]. Nearest-rank VaR80 = 4; worst-20% CVaR80 = 8 (USDm).
Loss = max(0, −NPV); a quantile differs from the mean of a chosen tail
Loss VaR80 USD4m; tail CVaR80 USD8m
Declare discrete tie treatment: mean(loss ≥ VaR) would be USD6m here, a different convention.
Stress code uses mean(loss ≥ 95% quantile). Its chosen continuous generator has negligible ties.
17: Each source loses USD10m with chosen probability 0.2. A shared port produces joint loss USD20m with probability 0.2; independent joint probability is 0.04.
Equal individual average losses can conceal different joint tail exposures
Expected total loss USD4m in both; joint tail differs
Chosen probabilities illustrate dependence. Country flags do not remove a shared crop season or port.
A different basin without a different port can leave route exposure unchanged.
18: Subtract the counterfactual change from the treated change
Parallel trends and no material spillovers are required. Four chosen means cannot support an estimated interval.
At USD2 contribution/unit, gross incremental contribution is USD40 before service and pilot cost.
19: Incremental contribution 120 − service 20 − trade 10 − cannibalisation 10 = 80. Marketing spend 40. Net ROMI = (80 − 40)/40 = 100%.
Net incremental contribution after marketing / marketing spend
All inputs are chosen currency-thousands. Use a paid-sales counterfactual and full incremental costs.
If contribution after other costs is only 40, net ROMI is zero. Multi-year proposals need NPV.
20: Good state p=0.5: investment NPV 10; bad state p=0.5: −8; wait 0. Best prior EV=1; perfect-information EV=5; less study 1 and delay 0.5 gives net gain 2.5.
Optimal decision value after information less before information, study and delay costs
A perfect study is an upper bound. Do not add its benefit again to a policy that already includes learning.
An imperfect pilot may be worth less than its cost; keep the wait option.
21: The managed owned template reaches zero NPV at 104,862 initial annual order tonnes. The current 100,000t base needs 4.86% more initial orders.
Solve the full NPV root and monitor the mechanism that moves it
The threshold depends on cost, hurdle, tax and capacity; volume cannot repair a negative unit contribution.
Cost, FX or commissioning shocks shift the boundary. Monitor orders together with cash.
22: Country A: demand 200kt, capture 50kt, unit contribution USD20, fixed USD0.7m → EBITDA USD0.3m. B: demand 100kt, capture 40kt, contribution USD40 → USD0.9m.
Delivered units × unit contribution less fixed cost, then full cash-flow valuation
B has 3 times EBITDA despite half the category size
A and B are fictional teaching cases. Chosen capex USD5m vs USD2m and NWC USD2m vs USD0.5m further favour testing B.
Before capital differences, A overtakes B above 80kt captured at USD20/t while B stays at 40kt.
